page: OVHcloud b3-64-flex is a general-purpose virtual machine operating on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 core-to-thread topology, avoiding multi-tenant resource contention. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local primary storage is bundled with a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface provides a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration does not include a GPU accelerator, nor does it supply complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which must be routed or allocated separately if required.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and upper-quartile PassMark memory throughput. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench compilation, static web serving throughput, and database transaction tests align within average tier distributions. While the bundled NVMe storage delivers low-latency performance, its 50 GB capacity necessitates external storage attachments for high-volume data. The b3-64-flex is suited for general web serving, software build pipelines, API backends, and moderate in-memory caching layers.
description: The OVHcloud b3-64-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance delivering 16 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Built with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, it eliminates hyperthreading overhead and pairs compute resources with 64.0 GB of RAM at a 4.0 GB per core ratio. Bundled hardware features include a 50 GB local NVMe SSD and a 4 Gbps network baseline, without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate strong single-core execution on stress-ng and high multi-threaded decompression throughput alongside solid memory subsystem metrics, while static web serving and PassMark database operations fall in the middle tier. Given its modest local storage footprint, the instance serves effectively as a host for continuous integration runners, web application clusters, microservices, and medium-scale caching databases.
